connector.why: Shares Genesis 28:11 and the arvit derashah only; its theme (Yaakov going out in safety, the Midrash on "az telech lavetach") is different. Not used.
Same Midrash (mi gilah lo she-shmi shemesh): Yaakov = sun, Knesses Yisrael = moon receiving from him. Used.
Same Midrash on chevel nachalaso (fewer than three strands) and Yaakov as the sum of the Avos (Zohar I 207a). Used.
From the Mafteach lead on BR 68:10. Yaakov the sun renews the moon (Knesses Yisrael). Used.
Ishbitz–Radzin: on Vayifga baMakom, Yaakov is the purpose of creation (= 2.26). Used.
The Mafteach lists it under Genesis 28:11–13, but it concerns Amalek and imagination; it shares only the dream verse. Not used.

found.why: Vayalen sham = a place of darkness; ki va hashemesh = shemesh u-magen through vayifga (prayer and viduy). The same move from darkness to light through teshuvah and prayer.
Vayifga = cleaving to holiness where there was no sunlight; arvit = finding the good point in the night.
Arvit = praying wholeheartedly in distress; Yaakov was "in the place of darkness".

found.ref: Beit Aharon, Teachings on Torah and Holidays, R' Aharon (the Second) of Karlin, Genesis, Chanukah 32
found.why: Ki va hashemesh = the sun goes into the moon, which receives from it; Yaakov called Sun (same Midrash).
